note: Single source of truth for every pricing coefficient used by PaintPricing. Consumed by the Next.js app via lib/catalog/index.ts and by the WordPress theme via the generated build (scripts/build-catalog.mjs). Do not hardcode coefficients anywhere else. Values marked source:'resolved' replaced two conflicting values; see DIVERGENCES.md.
keyPolicy: Entry keys are CANONICAL and are persisted inside saved quote payloads (QuoteItem.templateKey). Never rename a key. To rename a label, change 'label'. The 'aliases' array carries legacy or theme-side names that resolve to this entry.

pricing.minimumJobChargeNote: Conventional interior minimum. Without a floor the calculator returns numbers like 118 dollars for 30 linear feet of crown molding, which no painter would accept as a standalone visit. Applies to the job total, not per item.

living-room.label: Living room
spec: Usually the largest painted space in a house, and often the one with the highest ceiling.
Open plan rooms carry more wall area than the number of walls suggests, because there are fewer doorways breaking up the runs.

dining-room.label: Dining room
dining-room.note: Often has chair rail or wainscoting.
spec: Frequently has a chair rail, picture rail or wainscoting. Raise the trim footage to include it, since panelled walls are much slower than flat ones.
Often shares an opening with the living room, so the two are usually quoted together.

master-bedroom.label: Master bedroom
master-bedroom.note: Primary bedrooms with closets or bath access.
spec: Larger than a secondary bedroom and usually has more doors, since closets and an ensuite both add casing.
Walk in closets are normally quoted as a separate small room rather than folded into the bedroom.

standard-bedroom.label: Bedroom
spec: The most commonly quoted single room, and the usual reference point for a per room price.
Two windows and one door is typical. Each door and window is deducted from wall area and priced separately if painted.

kitchen.label: Kitchen
kitchen.note: Cabinets excluded. Trim is usually heavier here.
spec: Walls and trim only. Cabinets are priced per door and drawer front and are a different job.
The ceiling is excluded by default, because cabinets and appliances often make masking impractical.
Heavier trim than most rooms, plus a lot of cutting in around backsplash and cabinet runs.

bathroom.label: Bathroom
spec: Small area but high labor density. Cutting in around tile, mirrors, vanities and fixtures is most of the time on the job.
Usually takes a moisture resistant satin or semi gloss, which costs more per gallon than a flat wall paint.
The smallest rooms are where a minimum job charge matters most, since setup and cleanup do not scale down.

hallway.label: Hallway
hallway.note: Long trim runs and lots of door casing.
spec: Modest wall area but long trim runs and a lot of door casing, and casing is slow work.
Three doors of casing can outweigh the wall area entirely, which is why hallways cost more than people expect.
Stairwells attached to a hallway need staging or ladder work and are quoted separately.

home-office.label: Home office
home-office.note: Spare room converted to a workspace.
spec: Comparable to a secondary bedroom. Adjust the dimensions, since converted spare rooms vary widely.
Built in shelving is closer to cabinet work than wall work and is not included in a walls and trim estimate.

laundry-room.label: Laundry room
laundry-room.note: Small utility space, often semi gloss.
spec: Small utility space, normally finished in semi gloss or a moisture resistant paint.
Painting behind the washer and dryer means moving them, which is access time rather than painting time.

custom.label: Custom room
custom.note: Start from a blank room and adjust everything.
spec: A blank room. Enter your own dimensions, trim footage and openings.

siding.label: Siding
siding.note: Main body of the house. Lap, vinyl, or hardboard.
spec: Sprays roughly three times faster than it brushes, which is where most of the cost difference on an exterior lives.

stucco.label: Stucco
stucco.note: Rough texture. Absorbs significantly more paint than siding.
spec: Texture holds far more paint than flat siding, so coverage per gallon is much lower.
Usually sprayed then back rolled so the coating is pushed into the texture rather than bridging over it.

brick.label: Brick
brick.note: Highly absorbent. Masonry primer usually required first.
spec: The most absorbent exterior surface here. The first coat largely disappears into the face.
Masonry primer is effectively mandatory, and painted brick is very difficult to reverse.

trim-fascia.label: Trim and fascia
trim-fascia.note: Window casings, corner boards, fascia board. Slow ladder work.
spec: Costs far more per square foot than siding because production rate, not area, drives the labor.
Almost entirely ladder work on anything above a single storey.

soffit.label: Soffit
soffit.note: Underside of eaves. Overhead work, slower than siding.
spec: Overhead work, so slower than siding of the same area.

doors.label: Exterior doors
doors.note: Approximately 21 sq ft per door face. Becomes unit priced in P2.
spec: Approximately 21 sq ft per door face. Becomes properly unit priced once the unit basis ships.

garage-door.label: Garage door
spec: Panelled doors have many more cut lines than a flush door of the same area.

shutters.label: Shutters
shutters.note: Approximately 15 sq ft per shutter, 8 shutters default.
spec: Usually removed and sprayed flat, which is faster than coating them in place.

deck-porch.label: Deck or porch
deck-porch.note: Floor area. Stain or solid color. Railings slow this down sharply.
spec: Floor area only. Railings and spindles are separate and are far slower per square foot.

fence.label: Fence
fence.note: Both sides if accessible. Stain or paint.
spec: Enter the area for both sides if both are being coated.

custom-exterior.label: Custom surface
spec: Generic fallback rates. Use a specific surface where one exists.

cabinets.label: Kitchen cabinets
spec: Priced per door and drawer front, not by wall area. A 24 front kitchen is a different job from a 40 front kitchen regardless of room size.
The per front figure covers the front plus its share of the box and face frame, which are painted at the same time and are easy to forget when bidding.
Degreasing and sanding are the bulk of the labor. Cabinet failures are almost always adhesion failures from skipped prep.
Usually sprayed for finish quality, which means removing doors, labelling hinges and setting up a spray area.
cabinets.note: Priced per door and drawer front, not by wall area. A 24 front kitchen is a different job from a 40 front kitchen regardless of room size.

interior-doors.label: Interior doors
spec: Priced per door, counting both faces plus edges. Roughly 40 sq ft of painted area per door.
A six panel door takes noticeably longer than a flush door because every panel edge is cut in by hand.
Door casing is trim and is measured separately by the foot.
interior-doors.note: Priced per door, counting both faces plus edges. Roughly 40 sq ft of painted area per door.

baseboard.label: Baseboard
spec: Measured by the foot along the wall. Caulking the top edge is what makes baseboard look finished and is most of the prep.
Tall or profiled baseboard covers more area per foot and takes longer to cut in.
baseboard.note: Measured by the foot along the wall. Caulking the top edge is what makes baseboard look finished and is most of the prep.

crown-molding.label: Crown molding
spec: Slower per foot than baseboard because it is overhead work on a ladder with two cut lines, one to the wall and one to the ceiling.
Profiled crown holds more paint per foot than a simple cove.
crown-molding.note: Slower per foot than baseboard because it is overhead work on a ladder with two cut lines, one to the wall and one to the ceiling.

wainscoting.label: Wainscoting
spec: Panelled walls take far longer than flat walls of the same area. Every panel has inside corners that are cut in by brush.
Priced by area, but the production rate is closer to trim than to wall.
wainscoting.note: Panelled walls take far longer than flat walls of the same area. Every panel has inside corners that are cut in by brush.

stair-spindles.label: Stair spindles
spec: Priced per spindle. Small area, very high labor, because every spindle is a full wrap by brush.
One of the most commonly underbid items in interior painting.
stair-spindles.note: Priced per spindle. Small area, very high labor, because every spindle is a full wrap by brush.

handrail.label: Handrail and banister
spec: Slow per foot. A handrail is a full wrap with a finish that has to be smooth to the touch, so it is usually sanded between coats.
handrail.note: Slow per foot. A handrail is a full wrap with a finish that has to be smooth to the touch, so it is usually sanded between coats.

window-sash.label: Window sash
spec: Priced per window. Divided lights multiply the time, since every muntin is cut in by hand.
Older windows may need reglazing before painting, which is separate work.
window-sash.note: Priced per window. Divided lights multiply the time, since every muntin is cut in by hand.

gutters-downspouts.label: Gutters and downspouts
spec: Measured by the foot. Ladder work throughout, which sets the production rate more than the surface does.
Aluminium and galvanised both need a bonding primer or the coating peels.
gutters-downspouts.note: Measured by the foot. Ladder work throughout, which sets the production rate more than the surface does.

parking-lot-striping.label: Parking lot striping
spec: Measured in linear feet of line, typically a 4 inch stripe. Layout time on a fresh lot is separate from painting time.
Stalls, arrows, ADA symbols and crosswalks are counted as units on top of the linear footage.
Traffic paint is a different product from architectural paint, with its own coverage and cure time.
parking-lot-striping.note: Measured in linear feet of line, typically a 4 inch stripe. Layout time on a fresh lot is separate from painting time.

parking-stalls.label: Parking stalls
spec: Priced per stall, which is the unit commercial clients actually ask for a number on.
A standard single stripe stall is about 18 to 20 linear feet of line.
parking-stalls.note: Priced per stall, which is the unit commercial clients actually ask for a number on.

curb-painting.label: Curb painting
spec: Measured by the foot. Face and top of the curb are both coated, which is why the area per foot is high for a linear item.
Fire lane red and handicap blue are regulated colours in most jurisdictions.
curb-painting.note: Measured by the foot. Face and top of the curb are both coated, which is why the area per foot is high for a linear item.

quoteTerms: Quote valid for 7 days from issue date.
Pricing is based on visible conditions at the time of estimating.
Uncovered repairs, water damage, or change requests are billed separately.

bases.area: Priced by square footage. Walls, ceilings, siding, floors.
bases.linear: Priced by the foot. Trim, fence, striping, curb, pipe.
bases.unit: Priced per item. Doors, windows, cabinet fronts, spindles, stalls.
bases.system: Multi layer coating systems with per layer coverage and cure windows. Epoxy, industrial.
bases.prep: Prep is the scope rather than a multiplier. Washing, blasting, stripping, repair.
bases.crewday: Priced by crew days and mobilization rather than by measurement.
bases.dft: Industrial film build from solids by volume against target dry film thickness.

costStack.note: Layers 4 to 7 of the cost stack. The engine previously priced materials, sundries and direct labor only, which answers what a job consumes but not what to charge for it. Every figure here is a starting default a painter is expected to replace with their own.

laborBurden.note: Applied on top of the base wage to get a loaded hourly cost. Typical range is 25 to 45 percent depending on state and trade classification. Pricing off the raw wage is the most common way a small painting firm loses money without noticing.

overhead.note: Rent, insurance, admin, software, sales and vehicles, as a share of revenue. Recovered across all billable work rather than marked up on paint. Small painting firms typically sit between 15 and 25 percent.

profit.note: Net profit target after overhead. Distinct from gross margin. Price is derived as cost divided by one minus the margin, never cost times one plus the margin.

mobilization.note: Drive time, load in and load out. A default starting figure, not a published rate. Set the per mile figure to whatever your own vehicle cost works out to.

equipmentDayRates.note: Indicative daily rental. Regional rates vary widely, so treat these as placeholders until replaced with local quotes.

accessMultiplier.note: Production slows with height and access difficulty. Applied to labor hours, not to materials.
